messages:
alex: Heads up — saw a 12-18% throughput drop on an L40S rack after flipping the FP8 kernels into canary. p50 jittered too. Traces show the kernel selector oscillating between a TE-optimized FP8 path and an INT8 fallback on larger seqs.

maya: Which model / seq distribution? any repro?

alex: Model is redwood-7b-openq (open weights we onboarded). Traffic was mostly 1-512, batches 1-8. Quick trace excerpt below: 
```
{
  "step": 42,
  "kernel": "fp8_qgemm_te_fused",
  "time_ms": 0.92,
  "fallbacks": ["int8_qgemm_slowpath"],
  "kv_cache_evictions": 3
}
```

dmitri: I've seen this pattern on H100 when calibration used per-tensor scales vs per-channel. FP8 TE kernels assume per-channel/learned scaling in some codegens; mismatch can force extra dequant/dequant->requant paths which kills throughput.

jin: Try forcing the transformer engine config to prefer the stable FP8 kernels (we have a flag) and extend the kernel-selector hysteresis. e.g. `--te-fp8-stable=1 --selector-hysteresis-ms=250`.

sam: Also check batching heuristics — if KV cache misses create microbatch variance selectors see different occupancy and choose different kernels. Pinning kernel choice during warmup often helps.

ci-bot: canary: fp8-enable-2026-03-17 deployed to rack-l40s-3 -> rollback queued (reason: node-level regression alert)

maya: Commands I ran locally: 
```
rd-prof --trace --route redwood-7b-openq --seq 512 --batch 4 --kernels --warmup 200
```
That produced a high kernel-switch rate when starting from cold cache.

alex: Repro steps we used in lab: synthetic workload seq=512 batch=4 repeated 1k times. With cold KV cache the selector flip rate > 2x and avg step time increased. With warmed cache it stabilizes.

dmitri: Mitigations to try: 1) re-run FP8 calibration with a tail-aware collector (I think current calib under-sampled the tails), 2) bump selector stability threshold, 3) if immediate fix needed, fall back to INT8 for specific matmuls for seq>384.

jin: Also worth trying: disable per-op auto-requantization path in the TE for the suspect matmuls. That's `--te-disable-auto-requant` in staging.

sam: I'll open a short experiment ticket and schedule a canary that forces the stable FP8 kernel for 6h and compare latency/throughput + cost. Ticket: ENGRT/2478004444-fp8-stable-canary.

alex: Pasting a tiny selector log (human-friendly): 
```
[2026-03-17T14:12:01Z] selector: route=redwood-7b-openq seq=512 batch=4 choose=fp8_qgemm_te_fused
[2026-03-17T14:12:01Z] selector: occupancy=0.45 fallback_thresh=0.6 -> switched to int8_qgemm_slowpath
[2026-03-17T14:12:02Z] kv: miss route=redwood-7b-openq key=abc123 evict=1
[2026-03-17T14:12:02Z] selector: occupancy=0.72 hysteresis_counter=1 choose=fp8_qgemm_te_fused
```

maya: SGTM. @dmitri can you own the re-calibration run? @jin can you add selector tunables to the canary config? If we get stable numbers we can roll to more racks. :thumbsup:

dmitri: I can start a calibration job tonight with the tail-weight flag (`--calib-tail-weight=0.12`) and the new collector, will post results in this thread.

jin: I'll add the flags to the canary config and coordinate with Sam.

sam: I'll coordinate the canary window and monitor the route metrics + cpu/gpu occupancy. I'll post dashboards soon.

alex: thanks everyone — main goal: avoid knee-jerk rollback, find whether it's selector hysteresis + calib sampling or an actual kernel perf bug on L40S. We should have initial numbers by EOD tomorrow.
